property.title: Array-index safety for coefficient-wise in-place addition loop
property.candidate_statement: Under assumptions that r and b each designate a valid mlk_poly object, every access performed by mlk_poly_add stays within coeffs[0..MLKEM_N-1]; in particular, the single loop only reads and writes r->coeffs[i] and b->coeffs[i] for 0 <= i < MLKEM_N, with MLKEM_N = 256.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: for (i = 0; i < MLKEM_N; i++) ... r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]);
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The implementation uses index i only while i is strictly less than MLKEM_N and accesses coeffs at index i.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: typedef struct { int16_t coeffs[MLKEM_N]; } MLK_ALIGN mlk_poly;
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The accessed arrays have extent MLKEM_N within mlk_poly.
The concrete loop bound and array length are 256.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: n denotes the integer 256... an element f of R_q ... represented ... by the array (f0, f1, … , f255) in Z_q^256.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: A 256-coefficient representation matches the implementation loop extent.

required_assumptions: r points to a valid allocated object of type mlk_poly.
b points to a valid allocated object of type mlk_poly.
CBMC harness models complete mlk_poly objects rather than undersized buffers.
property.expected_artifact_type: standard_cbmc_harness with object-allocation assumptions and bounds assertions
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not claim coefficient arithmetic correctness.
Does not claim modular reduction or canonical output range.
Does not claim anything about callers beyond valid object shape.
property.uncertainty: Low; this is directly supported by the loop bound and struct definition.
limitations: Relies on harness assumptions for pointer validity.
Outside-CBMC runtime builds do not enforce these assumptions automatically.
